html:
SMTO-EXE-0040 — A command is waiting for someone to type an answer

GUID: 90fc6424-20e7-4f31-bab0-cd23f8862a63
Slug: terminal-input-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • A command stopped to ask a question, such as a password or a yes/no prompt, and nobody could answer it there. The command may have started before it asked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the step shows Waiting for terminal input and a workspace terminal is open, type the answer there, or select Let agent handle. The command continues as soon as it gets its answer.
  2. If this was a scheduled or background task, ask SMTO in the conversation to use a version of the command that doesn't stop to ask questions. Background tasks have no terminal where anyone can type an answer.
  3. Before running the command again, open the step and read its output to see how far it got. The command may have done some work before it stopped to ask, and repeating it could do that work twice.

What success looks like

  • The command finishes and the step shows its output without waiting for input.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't put passwords into the conversation to get past a prompt.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A captured or background command required interactive terminal input, or no trusted Agent UI or background terminal context was attached to supply it.

What this means

  • The captured/background execution path detected an interactive-input requirement or lacked the trusted terminal context needed for continuation. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The captured/background execution path detected an interactive-input requirement or lacked the trusted terminal context needed for continuation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect whether the process already started, its retained input request and the trusted terminal availability; do not launch a duplicate just to obtain a prompt.

How to fix it

  • Check the step metadata (terminal_input_required, terminal_context_required, background_task) from ShellExecutor._collect / shell_launch.missing_terminal. Provide a trusted terminal context (workspace terminal for foreground runs, a background terminal for scheduled or durable tasks) or make the command non-interactive; inspect the cancelled process's partial effects before starting a replacement.
  • Open an appropriate trusted terminal context and use the existing continuation flow if supported. Inspect the current process before starting another command.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation continues through a supported trusted terminal or is settled before replacement work.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
